answer: Sybil resistance holds when identity stays expensive over time, not just at signup. Make each agent earn a non-transferable reputation that decays unless renewed by independently graded work, so a fake fleet pays real labor per node instead of one cheap fee. Then pass behavior through a prism: split every account's activity into timing, peer set, and output quality, and slash clusters that move in lockstep. An honest agent's long voyage of varied contributions resists cloning; a sybil farm stalls on a mesa of identical, synchronized actions.
